answers.core: Doing this in GDScript would essentially require porting the entire shader preprocessor to GDScript. It would also require extending `Material` to essentially reimplement `ShaderMaterial` with the extra property.
answers.workaround: It might be possible by having a proxy shader that just makes a bunch of defines and then includes a common include file. However, I don't think `shader_type` and `render_mode` can be placed inside an include file. It also requires creating a shader file for each variant, so while it reduces code duplication, it is still not very user friendly.

title: Specify shader preprocessor definitions in material
